title: Diatom DNA library preparation
author: Cecile Chardon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bd94i98w

steps.title: Prepare fresh primer stocks
steps.instruction: Make 10 µM primer stocks for all forward (Diat_rbcL_708F_1_P5, Diat_rbcL_708F_2_P5, Diat_rbcL_708F_3_P5) and reverse (R3_1_P7, R3_2_P7) primers using the sequences provided; calculate the total volume needed for all samples, aliquot to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles and store aliquots at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Forward primer sequences: Diat_rbcL_708F_1 – AGGTGAAGTAAAAGGTTCWTACTTAAA; Diat_rbcL_708F_2 – AGGTGAAGTTAAAGGTTCWTAYTTAAA; Diat_rbcL_708F_3 – AGGTGAAACTAAAGGTTCWTACTTAAA.
Reverse primer sequences: R3_1 – CCTTCTAATTTACCWACWACTG; R3_2 – CCTTCTAATTTACCWACAACAG.
Add the Illumina adapter tails (P5: CTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT; P7: GGAGTTCAGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCT) to the 5’ end of each primer as shown in the table.

steps.title: Make equimolar primer mix and dilute
steps.instruction: Combine equal volumes of the five 100 µM primers to obtain an equimolar mix at 100 µM, then dilute 1:10 with molecular‑grade water to a 10 µM working mix; aliquot and store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Mix 1 volume of Diat_rbcL_708F_1_P5 (100 µM), 1 volume of Diat_rbcL_708F_2_P5 (100 µM) and 1 volume of Diat_rbcL_708F_3_P5 (100 µM) for the forward mix.
Mix 1 volume of R3_1_P7 (100 µM) and 1 volume of R3_2_P7 (100 µM) for the reverse mix.
Combine forward and reverse mixes as required for the PCRs.
Dilute the 100 µM mix 1 part mix + 9 parts water to obtain a 10 µM mix; ensure the final volume is sufficient for all reactions, aliquot, and keep at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare PCR‑1 master mix
steps.instruction: On the dedicated DNA‑work station, assemble a master mix for all samples (including 1 negative, 1 positive and 1 security control) using the volumes below; vortex, brief centrifuge, keep on refrigerated rack, and add Taq polymerase last.

substeps.instruction: Molecular‑grade water – 15.6 µL per sample
10 X PCR buffer – 2.5 µL per sample
dNTP mix (2.5 mM) – 0.2 µL per sample (final 0.2 mM)
BSA (10 mg/mL) – 1.25 µL per sample (final 0.5 mg/mL)
Primer F (10 µM) – 0.5 µL per sample (final 0.5 µM)
Primer R (10 µM) – 0.5 µL per sample (final 0.5 µM)
TaKaRa LA Taq® DNA polymerase (5 U/µL) – 0.15 µL per sample (0.75 U)
Vortex the mixture slowly, centrifuge briefly, keep on a refrigerated rack.
Add the Taq polymerase as the last component, pipetting slowly because the solution is viscous.

steps.title: Dispense master mix and add DNA
steps.instruction: Distribute 24 µL of the master mix into each well of 8‑tube strips, then add 1 µL of template DNA (or control) to reach a 25 µL final volume; vortex and centrifuge before cycling.

substeps.instruction: Use the same tip to dispense the master mix into multiple tubes if desired.

Add 1 µL extracted DNA (maximum 25 ng/µL) to each reaction. For the negative control add 1 µL molecular‑grade water. For the positive control add 1 µL DNA from a diatom culture or a previously amplified environmental sample.
If the DNA concentration is lower than 25 ng/µL, increase the DNA volume (e.g., 3 µL) and reduce water accordingly (e.g., 13.6 µL) to keep the total at 25 µL.
If the DNA concentration exceeds 25 ng/µL, dilute the extract to 25 ng/µL before adding 1 µL.
Close the strips, vortex the tube/DNA mixture slowly, and perform a brief centrifugation.

steps.title: Run PCR‑1 thermal program
steps.instruction: Place the strips in a thermal cycler and run the following program; do not exceed 40 cycles.

substeps.instruction: 95 °C for 5 min (1 cycle)
95 °C for 1 min (33 cycles)
54 °C for 1 min (33 cycles)
72 °C for 1 min (33 cycles)
72 °C for 5 min (1 cycle)
Hold at 10 °C
Note: cycle number may be increased up to a maximum of 40, but higher numbers should be avoided to limit nonspecific amplification and bias.

steps.title: Pool and store PCR‑1 products
steps.instruction: Combine the triplicate PCR‑1 reactions for each sample to obtain at least 50 µL of product with a minimum concentration of 30 ng/µL; place the pooled products in a 96‑well plate (column‑wise, no empty wells) sealed with adhesive film, and store as described.

substeps.instruction: Work in a dedicated amplicon‑handling room with dedicated pipettes and a UV‑treated DNA workstation.
After pooling, keep the plate at +4 °C for up to one week while processing other samples.
Transfer the plate to –20 °C for longer storage.
Thaw the pooled products 2–3 days before plate preparation; keep them on ice during handling.

steps.title: Prepare 96‑well plate with pooled products
steps.instruction: On the dedicated DNA workstation, clean the area, UV‑irradiate for 15 min, then pipette 52 µL of each pooled PCR‑1 product into the mapped wells of a Get‑PlaGe‑specified 96‑well plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a plate map and write the plate name on the plate.
Thaw the PCR‑1 product pools, vortex gently, and centrifuge briefly.
Place the pools in a rack in the correct order.
Using a new tip for each sample, pipette 52 µL of the appropriate pool into the designated well; fill the plate column‑wise.
Use a fresh tip box for each plate and discard each pool tube after its use.
Seal the plate with the recommended adhesive film, place the sealed plate in a bag, and store at +4 °C (maximum 2–3 days) before shipment.

steps.title: Ship sealed plate
steps.instruction: Package the bagged plate in an insulated box that maintains 0 °C–4 °C, ship within 1–2 days (preferably before Wednesday), and notify the platform.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the box contains sufficient cooling material to keep the temperature between 0 °C and +4 °C.
Dispatch the shipment within the required 1–2 day window.
Send an email to the Get‑PlaGe platform with the required Excel spreadsheet documenting the samples.
